others.route: Written approval of the Immigration Board

note: American Samoa: its immigration law is its own (A.S.C.A. Title 41), not the United States' (the us list isn't kept). No alien may seek or take employment without the Immigration Board's prior written approval (41.0410), on a resident sponsor (41.0408); an alien is anyone not a national or citizen of the United States (41.0202), so a US passport works freely and every other, Micronesia's, the Marshall Islands' and Palau's included, needs the approval. Guest workers under chapter 09 aren't modelled apart, and no days of work without approval are named. Read in the American Samoa Bar Association's copy of the Code Annotated.

sources.title: American Samoa Bar Association, A.S.C.A. 41.0410 Employment of aliens-Penalty
sources.said: (a) No person may knowingly employ any alien without written approval of the Board before the person commences work. ... (b) No alien may seek employment or become employed without prior written approval of the Board.

sources.title: American Samoa Bar Association, A.S.C.A. 41.0202 Definitions
sources.said: “Alien” means all persons who are not nationals or citizens of the United States of America.
